title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page, §5): this section gives a universal characterization of the pro-schematic envelope (pro-unipotent or pro-quasi-unipotent completion) of a discrete group, written here as a stylised G and below as 𝔊. For a group scheme G locally of finite presentation over a base S, a homomorphism H→G is called unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) if it lands in unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) elements, which can be checked fibre by fibre. A homomorphism 𝔊→Γ(G/S) is called unipotent if the corresponding map from the constant group scheme 𝔊_S→G is.

What this page does:
1. The envelope Env(𝔊) is first built over a 'universal base' S_0, presumably Spec Z, or Spec Q in the strictly unipotent case. It is a filtrant projective system (𝔊_i) of affine S_0-group schemes, which is base-changed to any S to give Env_S(𝔊).
2. Since the transition maps are affine, the projective limit exists as an affine group scheme: LEnv(𝔊) = lim 𝔊_i. Limits commute with base change, which gives (57): LEnv_S(𝔊) = LEnv(𝔊) ×_{S_0} S ≅ lim Env_S(𝔊).
3. (58) For G locally of finite presentation over S, morphisms from the projective limit into G are the colimit of morphisms from the stages (the EGA IV §8 limit formalism): Hom_{pro-gr/S}(Env_S(𝔊), G) := colim_i Hom(𝔊_{i,S}, G) ≅ Hom(LEnv_S(𝔊), G).
4. (59 bis) The canonical maps 𝔊_{S_0}→𝔊_i give a homomorphism from the constant group scheme 𝔊_{S_0} to LEnv(𝔊). Base change gives (59): 𝔊_S → LEnv_S(𝔊).

Next page: composing (58) with restriction along (59) gives (61): Hom_{pro-S-gr}(Env_S 𝔊, G) → Hom_gr(𝔊, G(S)). The stated theorem is that this map is injective, with image the unipotent (or quasi-unipotent) homomorphisms. Possibly extra hypotheses are imposed 'to simplify', e.g. S noetherian and G of finite type.

In modern terms: Env_S(𝔊) represents the functor of unipotent representations of 𝔊 in arbitrary locally finitely presented S-group schemes, uniformly over all bases. It is a relative or integral Malcev (unipotent) completion, defined once over the universal base and base-changed. This page is purely formal; the substantive content (existence of the envelope over S_0 and density of the image of 𝔊) lies in the theorem on the next page.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The formal steps (57)-(59) are standard consequences of EGA IV §8 (limits with affine transition maps; Hom into locally finitely presented targets commutes with the limit).

Implicit gap: the injectivity claimed on the next page needs the image of 𝔊_S to be schematically dense in LEnv_S(𝔊) after arbitrary base change. That is not automatic over a general S (e.g. non-flat situations, mixed characteristic over Z) and is not argued here.

The status of 'unipotent' over Z or in characteristic p (where unipotent elements have p-power order) is not addressed on this page. The quasi-unipotent variant suggests awareness of this, but the universal base S_0 is not specified.

ideas.what: Pro-schematic envelope of a discrete group as a projective system of affine group schemes over a universal base S_0, base-changed to arbitrary S
ideas.modern_name: Malcev / pro-unipotent completion (relative or integral version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Malcev (1949); Quillen (rational homotopy, 1969); Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); Hain (relative completion)
ideas.where_published: Motivated by the Longue Marche (1981) programme; the pro-algebraic envelope is evoked loosely in Esquisse d'un programme / Pursuing Stacks (schematization), but no detailed text is published as far as I know

ideas.what: Hom from a pro-object with affine transition maps into a locally finitely presented scheme equals Hom from its limit (58)
Universal property: homomorphisms from the envelope to G correspond bijectively to unipotent (resp. quasi-unipotent) homomorphisms 𝔊→G(S), for G locally of finite presentation over an arbitrary base
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of unipotent completion over a general base; quasi-unipotent completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Over a field of characteristic 0: standard (Deligne, Hain). Over general bases or Z: scattered later work, unsure of attribution

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up unipotent and quasi-unipotent envelopes of discrete groups over a universal base (apparently Z), with a universal property valid for group schemes over arbitrary bases S. Integral and mixed-characteristic unipotent completion, and especially a 'quasi-unipotent completion' adapted to monodromy, remain only partially developed in the literature.
missed.quote: d'où un système projectif de schémas en groupes affines sur S_0, donc sur S, noté Env_S(𝔊)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic versions of Malcev completion (integral schematization à la Toën, integral unipotent fundamental groups) are active topics. A clean base-change-compatible universal property, including a quasi-unipotent version, could be a useful framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is formal, but it documents Grothendieck working out a base-change-compatible (integral) unipotent and quasi-unipotent completion with an explicit universal property, in unpublished detail. The underlying notion (Malcev completion) is well known, so the novelty lies only in the generality of the base and in the quasi-unipotent variant.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'End'/'LEnd' (and 'Ext' on the next page) should read 'Env'/'LEnv' (enveloppe), consistent with the section title 'enveloppe pro-schématique'.
Page number at top likely reads '663' (or a similar three-digit number), not '66B'.
'si 𝔊 est unit[?] bilim[?]' is uncertain; the gist is a condition or construction giving the projective system of affine group schemes over S_0. The reading is not certain.
(58): the left side is Hom_{progr/S}(Env_S(𝔊), G), the right side is Hom(LEnv_S(𝔊), G), and the line below (marked '|| def') is colim_i Hom(𝔊_{i,S}, G).
'[-une-] [-...-] homom. canoniques' should read roughly 'qu'on a un homom. canonique'.
